The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- from the respondents for the injuries sustained by her in the road traffic accident that took place on 10.08.2024.
2.

The brief facts of the case of the petitioner as follows:
On 10-08-2024 at about 5.30 a.m. when she was pillion rider on the motor cycle bearing Reg. No. KA-06-HL-4273 along with one Kiran who was riding the motor cycle, at Tumkur- Bengaluru NH 48 road, Nandihalli village, Tumkur, at that time,
rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.HP-36-E-3372 came from opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner's vehicle, due to impact,
petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately, after the accident, petitioner was shifted to We care multi-speciality Hospital, wherein she was treated as inpatient.

It is stated that she has spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards treatment, medicine etc.,
3.
It is contended that prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy and was working as a Picker at Reliance packing and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, she is unable to do the work as she was doing earlier and lost income.
The accident in question was due to the rash and negligence of the rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.HP-36-E-3372.

Hence, the respondent No.2 being the owner and respondent No.1 being the insurer of the offending vehicle are Kavya B K vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57650475/
2 jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

The rider of the motor cycle had no driving licence to drive the vehicle involved in the accident.
The petition is bad for non joinder of owner and insurer of the motor bike as the rider of the motor bike baring No.KA-06-HL-4273 was responsible for the accident.

The rider of the motor bike bearing No.KA-06-HL-4273 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner which came on wrong side where the passing of he vehicle is prohibited and dashed against the motor vehicle driven by the 2nd respondent.
The police have registered a case against he rider of the motor bike bearing No.KA-06-HL-4273.

sentences.text: 10 . Issues No.1:

As per the case of the petitioner, on 10- 08-2024 at about 5.30 p.m. while she was proceeding on the motor cycle bearing Reg. No. KA-06-HL-4273 as a pillion rider on Tumkur-Bengaluru NH 48 road, Nandhihalli village, Tumkur, at that time, rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg. No. HP-36-E-3372 came from opposite direction without following traffic rules and regulations in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motor cycle in which petitioner was proceeding and as a result, she fell down and sustained injuries.

The petitioner in order to prove her case, got examined herself as PW.1 and reiterated the averments of the petition and got marked F.I.R, complaint, spot mahazar, IMV report, wound certificate, charge sheet, discharge summary as per Ex.P1 to 8.
11.

On the other hand, Respondent No.1 who is the insurer of the offending motorcycle bearing reg No. HP-36-E-3372 has denied the alleged negligence of the rider of the offending motorcycle and taken specific contention that the petitioner came on wrong side where the passing of the vehicle is prohibited in rash and negligently and dashed against the motorcycle of the Respondent No.2,
petitioner only solely responsible for the alleged accident.

12. According to the version of petitioner, the accident happened Tumkur-Bengaluru NH 48 road,
Nandhihalli village, Tumkur, at that time, the rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.HP-36-E-3372 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner's motor cycle and caused the accident.
It is pertinent to note that, the criminal law was set in motion on the same day of accident as per Ex.P.2.
Ex .P.1 FIR has its germane in Ex.P.2.
The document which sheds light on the factum of negligence are Ex.P.3 being the Spot Mahazar, conducted in the place of accident.
Ex. P.3
and Ex
. P4 which is the sketch prepared at the time of spot mahazar

and on perusal of the above said documents it clearly reflects that petitioner is the pillion rider and the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg No.KA- 06-HL-4273 went on wrong side where the passing of the vehicles are prohibited and also accident occurred towards South distance of 3 feet from the North edge of the road and also width of the road is 30 feet.
Both the vehicles riders without observing the on going vehicles on the road they dashed against each other.
Added more the contents of Ex.P5 which is the IMV report itself discloses that there are no mechanical defects whatsoever in the offending vehicle as well as petitioner's motorcycle.
Even the Chargesheet as per Ex.P7 was also filed as against the rider of the motor cycle in which petitioner was proceeding and also against the rider of the offending motorcycle/Respondent No.2.

When such is the case having regard to Ex.P3 to 5 coupled with Ex.P7 charge sheet it is crystal clear that, the accident happened because of rash and negligence driving by the Respondent No.1 as well as rider of the motor cycle in which Petitioner was proceeding.
13. It is true that both the vehicles and other users of the road are required to follow the traffic rules.

On proper perusal of the spot mahazer and sketch, it shows that rider of the motor cycle in which petitioner was proceeding came from opposite direction in one way road on wrong side where passing of vehicles is prohibited, in a negligent manner, on the other side the rider of the motorcycle bearing No. HP-36-E-3372 also came in negligent manner without observing the other vehicle, both the vehicles collided each other and accident occurred towards South from the North edge of the road at the distance of 3 feet, due to which both riders of the motorcycle fell-down along with motorcycles.

If both riders rode their vehicles in normal speed by observing on going vehicles on the Kavya B K vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57650475/
4 road, they might have avoided the accident and also if rider of the petitioner's vehicle had avoided the passing his motorcycle in wrong side and if he had taken little care and follow the traffic rules in the National highway road, might have avoided collision.

It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the incident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.

sentences.text: The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

15. The discussion supra makes it is abundantly clear that, the accident occurred due to the rash negligent riding by the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.HP-36-E-3372 and the rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-06-HL-4273 in which petitioner was proceeding as pillion rider has also contributed in occurrence of the said accident.

Hence contributory negligence is attributed on the rider of the offending motorcycle bearing Reg.No.HP-36-E-3372 and also by the rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-06- HL-4273 in the ratio of 40:60 respectively.

As such, I answer Issue No.1 as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
16. Issue No.2:

While answering issue No.1, I have already observed that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding by the offending motorcycle bearing Reg.No.HP- 36-E-3372 and also by the rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-06-HL-4273.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for the compensation.

17. LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS ON ACCOUNT OF PERMANENT DISABILITY:
The petitioner has not examined the doctor to prove the disability.
Hence, she is not entitled for compensation for loss of future income on account of permanent disability.

18. PAIN AND SUFFERINGS:
Petitioner has produced wound certificate at Ex.P6 which reveals that the petitioner has sustained simple injury.

Further the Ex.P8 Discharge Summary of We care multi-Speciality Hospital reveals that the petitioner has sustained injury i.e., soft tissue injury and right ulnar styloid fracture and was treated as an inpatient in the said hospital from 10-08-2024 to 12-08-2024 totally for a period of 3 days.

Considering these aspects, I deem it just and proper to award Rs.30,000/- towards Kavya B K vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57650475/
5 pain and sufferings.
19.

sentences.text: MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The petitioner has produced 13 medical bill worth Rs.34,269/- as per Ex.P9.
I have examined the said medical bills.

Since the petitioner was treated as inpatient and undergone treatment, there are no reasons to disbelieve the amount spent by the petitioner to the tune of Rs.34,269/- and she is entitled for the same.
20. ATTENDANT, CONVEYANCE, FOOD & NOURISHMENT AND OTHER INCIDENTAL EXPENSES:
As the petitioner was treated as an inpatient for a period of 3 days, certainly she might have spent amount towards conveyance, attendant charges, nourishing food and other incidental expenses and also at the time of subsequent follow up treatment.
Considering these aspects, I deem it proper to award Rs.20,000/- under this head.

21. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:
According to the petitioner, she was working as Picker at Reliance packing and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
But, the petitioner has not produced any document to show her income.
In the absence of document of income, the court has to consider the notional income of the petitioner.
The incident occurred during the year 2024.
Therefore, I deem it just and proper to consider the notional income of the petitioner as Rs.16,500/- p.m.
The evidence on record reveals that petitioner has sustained simple injury.
Considering the injuries sustained to the petitioner and treatment taken by her, she might not have attended her work at least for a period of three months.

Hence,
petitioner is entitled for the compensation of Rs.49,500/- on the above head.
22. LOSS OF AMENITIES IN LIFE/LIFE COMFORTS AND EXPECTANCY OF LIFE:
There is no evidence on record to show that petitioner has sustained the disability.
Therefore, she is not entitled for compensation on this head.

Thus in all, the petitioner is entitled for the compensation as here under:

The petitioner is claiming interest on the compensation amount.
The respondents have denied the same.

Our Hon'ble High Court in the case rendered in Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another (MFA.No.100090/2014 C/W MFA.No.25107/2013 dated 07.03.2018), has held that in the absence of any other law relating to interest on judgments, the MACT has to follow the provisions of Sec.34 of C.P.C and awarded interest @ 6% p.a.

24. Liability:

Regarding fixation of liability is concerned, I have already observed that the accident was taken place due to the negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.
KA-06-HL-4273 and rider of the offending motor cycle bearing Reg. No.HP-36-E-3372 in the ratio of 60:40 respectively.
There is no dispute with regarding to the ownership of the vehicles.
The respondent No.1 had admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.HP-36-E-3372.

It has to be noted that, the accident had occurred due to the negligence of rider of the motor cycle bearing No. KA-06-HL- 4273 and the petitioner has not made the owner and insurer of the said motor cycle as party to the proceedings.

Even though they are not made as a party, the owner of the said vehicle is bound to pay the compensation amount to the petitioner to an extent of 60% and the petitioner shall recover the same from him.

Further, the 1st respondent being the Insurer of offending motor cycle bearing No.HP-36-E-3372 shall indemnify the respondent No.2 in payment of remaining compensation amount of 40% to the petitioner.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative.
